findings: physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters: perfect hashtables can now use a bloom filter only when the build keys are sparse (count*4 <= range+1, computed in HUGEINT so it cannot overflow), and only as an exact BF. It is a general density rule, not tied to any table, column or literal. The normal CanUseBloomFilter guards (join type, build_side_has_filter, size ratio) still apply.

perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp FillExactBloomFilter: the filter inserts build_min, widened the same way TrySetExactBloomFilter widens it (int64 sign-extension or uint64), plus each set slot. These are the same slots the perfect HT uses. If the BF range and the HT statistics ever disagree, InsertExact sets exact_overflow, and the lookup in bloom_filter.cpp:181/233/267 then passes everything, so a mismatch makes the filter useless but never wrong. A dense build (all-valid bitmap) is handled by filling every slot, and the density gate rejects that case earlier anyway.

Parallel path: FinishBuild resets build_task_count and copies build_bits into bitmap_build_idx before FinalizeFilters and the push in FinishEvent, so the bitmap is complete when it is read. Serial path: the push happens after BuildPerfectHashTable. In the fallback to a regular hash join (duplicate keys), use_perfect_hash is false, so the push is skipped and the existing HT-finalize BF path runs as before. The deferred list is cleared, so nothing is pushed twice, and a half-filled BF is never pushed.

NULL keys never set bitmap bits. IS NOT DISTINCT FROM is excluded through NullValuesAreEqual in TrySetExactBloomFilter. Non-integer and 128-bit keys return false. I found no input that gives a wrong result.
Minor: the plain and perfect branches in FinalizeFilters repeat the same long condition. It is readable as is and does not block approval.
